info.title: Calculator API
info.description:
The calculator service does exact decimal arithmetic: `0.1 + 0.2` is `0.3`. When a result has to be rounded, such as `1 ÷ 3`, the response says so with `"exact": false`.

**Numbers are JSON strings**, in requests and responses, so no number passes through binary floating point. A JSON number as an operand is rejected with `INVALID_NUMBER`.

**Precision.** Every result keeps at most 34 significant digits, rounded half to even, in one rounding step. Inputs over the number limits are rejected, never rounded.

**Errors** all have one shape, `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`, and each code always comes with the same HTTP status. Clients should act on `code`; `message` is for people and may change.

| Status | Codes |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST`, `INVALID_NUMBER`, `WRONG_OPERAND_COUNT`, `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` |
| 405 | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` |
| 413 | `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` |
| 422 | `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`, `NEGATIVE_SQUARE_ROOT`, `INVALID_EXPONENT`, `OUT_OF_RANGE` |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, sent by the web container's nginx, never by the calculator |

Two of them can come from any request under `/api/`: a path there that is not listed below is `404 NOT_FOUND` (so is a path not in clean form, such as `/api/v1//calculate` or a trailing slash), and a method a listed `/api/` path does not accept is `405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, with an `Allow` header. Both are listed under each `/api/` operation. Paths outside `/api/` belong to the web container: the app, `/docs/` and its own `/healthz`.

**Request IDs.** Every response carries an `X-Request-ID` header. Send a well-formed one (1 to 64 letters, digits or hyphens) and it is kept; otherwise a new one is made. The service's log line for an API request carries the same ID.

post.description:
Runs one operation on its operands and returns the result as a decimal string.

| Operation | Operands | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add` | 2 | a + b |
| `subtract` | 2 | a − b |
| `multiply` | 2 | a × b |
| `divide` | 2 | a ÷ b. A zero divisor is `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`. |
| `percentage` | 2 | a% of b, which is a × b ÷ 100 |
| `power` | 2 | a to the power b. b must be a whole number from −1000 to 1000, checked by value, so `"2.0"` and `"-0"` are accepted; anything else is `INVALID_EXPONENT`. `0^0` is `1`, and zero to a negative power is `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`. |
| `sqrt` | 1 | the square root of a. A negative operand is `NEGATIVE_SQUARE_ROOT`. |

Every result follows the same number rules as an operand, so it can be sent back as one. A result outside the range is `OUT_OF_RANGE`.

The request examples below each have a response example of the same name, and a test sends every one of them to the service and checks that it gets exactly that response.

200.description: The result. `exact` is `false` when it was rounded.

sqrt.summary: Square root of 2, rounded to 34 digits

400.description: The request is malformed, an operand is not a valid number, the operand count is wrong for the operation, or the operation does not exist.

error.message: Operands must be strings, for example "0.1".
Operand 2 is not a valid number. Use a plain decimal such as "-12.5".

unknownKey.summary: A key other than operation and operands

error.message: The body must be one JSON object with exactly two keys: "operation" (a string) and "operands" (an array of strings).

unsupportedOperation.summary: An operation that does not exist

error.message: Unsupported operation "modulo". Supported operations: add, divide, multiply, percentage, power, sqrt, subtract.

413.description: The body is over 4 KiB (4096 bytes), or an operand is over 256 bytes or 34 significant digits. A body over 16 KiB never reaches the calculator: the web container's nginx answers it with the same code and its own message.

tooManyDigits.summary: An operand one digit over the limit

error.message: Operand 2 has more than 34 significant digits.
The request body is larger than 4096 bytes.

422.description: The request is well-formed, but the operation has no result for these operands.

error.message: Cannot raise zero to a negative power.

negativeSquareRoot.summary: Square root of a negative number

error.message: Cannot take the square root of a negative number.
The exponent must be a whole number from -1000 to 1000.

The result is outside the supported range of 1e-100 to 1e100.

get.summary: Check that the service is up
get.description:
Returns `{"status": "ok"}` while the process is running. It does no other work and is not logged.

Through the web container, `/healthz` is not forwarded: nginx answers it itself, with the same body, for its own container's health check. "Try it out" on this page therefore checks nginx, not the calculator.

CalculateRequest.description: Exactly these two keys, each once, matched case-sensitively. A missing, repeated or extra key, a body that is not one JSON object, or anything after the object is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. The whole body is at most 4 KiB (4096 bytes); a larger one is `413 INPUT_TOO_LARGE`.

operation.description: The operation to run. Another string is `400 UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`; a value that is not a string is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

operands.description: The operands, as strings. `sqrt` takes one; every other operation takes two, in the order the operation names them (`divide` is the first ÷ the second). The wrong count is `400 WRONG_OPERAND_COUNT`. An element that is not a string, such as the JSON number `0.1`, is `400 INVALID_NUMBER`; an `operands` that is not an array is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

result.description: The result. It follows the operand rules, so it can be sent back as an operand.

exact.description: `false` when the result was rounded to 34 significant digits, half to even. Always present.

Number.description:
A decimal number as a string. The rules are checked in this order:

1. At most 256 bytes of UTF-8. Longer is `413 INPUT_TOO_LARGE`. Length is checked before format, so a long run of non-ASCII characters gets 413, not `INVALID_NUMBER`.
2. A plain decimal: an optional minus sign, digits, and an optional fraction. No `+`, exponent, spaces, or leading or trailing point. Anything else is `400 INVALID_NUMBER`.
3. At most 34 significant digits, counted from the first non-zero digit to the last, so `0.00012` has 2 and `1200` has 2. More is `413 INPUT_TOO_LARGE`.
4. Zero, or a magnitude from 10⁻¹⁰⁰ up to, but not including, 10¹⁰⁰. Outside that is `422 OUT_OF_RANGE`.

Error.description: Every error response has this shape.

code.description: What went wrong, as a stable name. Act on this.

message.description: An explanation for people. It may change.

Error503.description: The code sent with status 503, by the web container's nginx only.

RequestId.name: X-Request-ID
RequestId.description: Optional. An ID for this request, to find its log line. A well-formed one is kept and sent back; anything else is replaced with a new one. Leave it empty to get a new ID for each request.
The request's ID: the incoming `X-Request-ID` if it was well-formed, otherwise a new one. The service's log line for an API request carries the same ID.

NotFound.description: Nothing is at this path, or the path is not in clean form. Any request can get this.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists, but not with this method. Any listed path can send this for a method it does not accept.

Allow.description: The methods the path accepts: `POST`, or `GET, HEAD`.

InternalError.description: A bug in the service. The cause is logged with the request ID; the message is always the same.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Sent by the web container's nginx, never by the calculator: the calculator could not be reached or did not answer in time. nginx sets `X-Request-ID` on it too.

error.message: The calculator service is unavailable. Try again shortly.
